verses.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.2: Should a wise man not speak? Should someone who has knowledge not respond?
verses.3: Does the Lord take pleasure in the just? Or if you are upright, does He accept your ways?
verses.4: Is it before you that He argues, that He comes to you in judgment?
verses.5: Is not your iniquity great, your sins without number?
verses.6: For you have taken pledges from your brothers in vain, and stripped the naked of their garments.
verses.7: You gave no water to the weary to drink, and you withheld bread from the hungry.
verses.8: You caused a man to take possession of land, and he who had no strength you made to dwell in it.
verses.9: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of orphans you broke.
verses.10: Therefore snares surround you, and sudden terror makes you panic.
verses.11: Or darkness, which you cannot see, and a flood of waters covers you.
verses.12: Does not God dwell in the heavens? Does He see the height of the stars, which He has exalted?
verses.13: And you say, "What does God know? He judges through the thick darkness."
verses.14: His clouds are a covering for Him, and He does not see; His circle in the heavens He walks.
verses.15: Does He keep the ancient path, which the wicked have walked?
verses.16: Those whose foundation was laid but not in time, whose foundations were washed away by a river.
verses.17: They said to God, "Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?"
verses.18: And He filled their houses with good things, and the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
verses.19: The righteous will see and rejoice, and the innocent will mock them.
verses.20: But if they are not destroyed, then fire will consume them.
verses.21: Return now, and you will be at peace with Him. Then your hope will come out in good.
verses.22: Take instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
verses.23: If you return to the Almighty, He will restore you, and remove iniquity far from your tent.
verses.24: Then you will set your treasure on the dust, and your gold in the rock of a stream.
verses.25: And the Almighty will be in your distress, and silver will be refined for you.
verses.26: Then you will delight in the Almighty, and lift your face to God.
verses.27: You will make a request to Him, and He will hear you. Your vows you will pay.
verses.28: You will decide on a matter, and it will be set before you. On your paths light will shine.
verses.29: For when you fall, you will say, "Exaltation!" and the eyes that are bowed will be rescued.
verses.30: He will deliver the innocent one, and you will be rescued by clean hands.

notes:
Notes
- v. 12: "the height of the stars" is a reference to their exalted position, not their physical height.
- v. 16: "whose foundation was laid but not in time" reflects the Hebrew text's metaphor for unstable or doomed foundations.
- v. 24: "gold in the rock of a stream" is a poetic metaphor for hidden or tested treasure.
- v. 25: "silver will be refined for you" uses "refined" to capture the metaphor of purification through trial.
